issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None, producing a malformed '.../latest/None/Packages/...' URL
issues.detail: When the arch regex doesn't match, the function returns None and the caller interpolates it directly into the URL via f-string with no termination check. A missing fact becomes a string-shaped fact flowing downstream as valid. Either raise on failure or have the caller refuse to continue; do not let None compose into a corrupt URL.

issues.description: nevra[0] uses the first character of the filename, not the package name's first letter, violating the koji path convention
issues.detail: The canonical koji layout requires the first letter of the package NAME, lowercased. nevra[0] takes the first char of the URL basename, which only matches by accident when the filename begins with the package name. Digit-prefixed names (e.g. '389-ds-base', '7zip') or any leading path segment silently produce a wrong subdir. State and assert the precondition, or compute the name properly.

issues.description: Arch is read from URL path scan instead of the NEVRA filename, creating two sources of truth that can disagree
issues.detail: Every RPM filename ends in .<arch>.rpm — the canonical value. Scanning the whole URL path with regex.search() returns the first match, so a path like /ppc64le-mirror/.../foo.x86_64.rpm misclassifies. Read the arch from the NEVRA filename suffix (or thread it in from the caller, which already knows it), not from wherever it happens to appear in the URL.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list and koji URL base are scattered constants with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The supported arch tuple in extract_arch_from_url is independent of the arches generate_main iterates over, and the koji base URL is a string literal embedded in logic. A change to either silently invalidates the other. Hoist to module-level constants (SUPPORTED_ARCHES, KOJI_URL_BASE) describing the koji repo layout as inspectable data.

issues.description: Race with koji-tagger and untestable-locally assumption live only in the PR body, not the code
issues.detail: The constructed URL is valid only after coreos-koji-tagger processes the merge commit — a temporal invariant the code never names. There is no stated invariant under which the URL is guaranteed to resolve, no detection, and the author concedes local testing is hard. Add a literate comment naming the race-with-tagger assumption and the precondition on input URLs.

issues.description: No unit test for a pure, deterministic URL-rewriting function whose correctness depends on string parsing
issues.detail: The function is trivially testable with a handful of representative URLs (coreos-pool passthrough, fedora x86_64, fedora-secondary ppc64le, digit-prefixed filename, arch-substring-in-path edge case). A 20-line test would catch the nevra[0], None-arch, and arch-misclassification issues above. The PR notes local testing is hard — all the more reason to test the parts that are local.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on REFUSED-IN-CURRENT-FORM. The patch substitutes string-mangling for correctness: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and composes into a literal 'None' URL segment, and nevra[0] indexes the filename's first char rather than the package name's first letter, both unstated preconditions. Arch is read from the URL path instead of the canonical NEVRA filename, creating two sources of truth that can disagree. Scattered constants, an unnamed race with koji-tagger, and absent unit tests compound the risk. Fix the silent-None and nevra[0] bugs, thread arch from the NEVRA, hoist constants, and add tests before landing.
